Subject: Pilot billing question — short/long mix and rounding behavior

Hi Markus / Marissa,

Thanks for the call earlier. Before we finalize the PO our finance team has two quick questions about how Redwood will meter the pilot so we can model cost:

1) Rounding / padding: For a mix of short interactive requests and occasional long context requests (examples below), does Redwood round up each request to a fixed slab? If so, what is the slab size for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints and for ephemeral sessions vs persistent KV-cache sessions.

2) Commit credits and model switches: We plan to pin a smaller hosted deployment for development and then switch to a dedicated pool for production load. How do reserved commit credits apply during the switch window if the same conversation spans both environments? Do we get crediting for prefix tokens consumed while on hosted after the switch?

Example traffic (attached CSV):
- 70% of calls: single-turn prompts, median 95 tokens total (prompt+response)
- 25% of calls: short multi-turn threads, average 420 tokens active context
- 5% of calls: ingestion/analytics prompts, up to 18k tokens

Procurement would like a short note we can include with the PO clarifying the math — rounding approach, minimum billing per call (if any), and any amortization windows you use.

Appreciate the quick clarification,

—Lena

Thanks for the clear examples, Lena — helpful. High level answers below, and Marissa / Kim will add the technical/ops details so you have a note for Procurement. Happy to turn this into a one-page appendix for the PO.

1) Rounding/padding: For our hosted text-generation API we meter at a 32-token quantum for non-streamed (batch) calls and at a 16-token quantum for streaming responses. However we also apply a minimum per-call floor of 48 tokens when requests are under 48 tokens (this prevents degenerate bookkeeping for microcalls). For persistent sessions that reuse KV cache, we amortize the prefix over a 60-second sliding window — subsequent calls that reuse the cached prefix in that window won’t be re-charged for the full prefix (they’re charged primarily for the delta).

2) Commit credits & environment switches: Reserved commit credits are tied to the customer account (not a physical node), so when you transfer traffic from hosted to Dedicated we prorate commit usage during the handover. If a conversation originated on hosted and later continues on Dedicated within the 60s amortization window, we treat the prefix as eligible for amortization on the receiving environment provided the request is authenticated under the same customer account and the model variant is compatible. We’ll note any edge cases (e.g., model family changes) in the appendix.

Action: Marissa — can you draft a one-paragraph appendix that shows sample math for the traffic buckets Lena shared? Kim — attach the pricing sheet and confirm the exact quantum numbers for the Dedicated pool (sometimes we minimize the floor there if there’s a reserved slot config).

-Markus

Hi Lena — appended below is the short table + a concise note you can paste under the PO. Kim also attached the pricing-sheet PDF for the deal.

Sample billed-token mapping (examples):
- 46 input+output tokens -> billed 48 (minimum floor)
- 95 tokens -> round up to nearest 32 -> 96 billed tokens
- 420 tokens -> rounded to nearest 32 -> 416 billed tokens (we bill the exact slabed total)
- 18,000 tokens -> we switch to chunked billing: the first 16k is billed as a large-context slab, any remainder is billed in 8k increments; so 18k -> 16k + 2k (rounded to 8k) = billed as 24k equivalent for that call.

Short PO appendix wording (one paragraph):
"Redwood bills generation calls using token quanta to simplify metering. Interactive (non-stream) calls are rounded to 32-token quanta with a 48-token minimum; streaming responses use 16-token quanta. Persistent sessions benefit from a 60-second amortization window for prefix reuse; if a session moves across deployment types under the same customer account within the amortization window, prefixes are eligible for amortization on the receiving environment. Very long single calls (>16k tokens) are chunked into 8k increments for billing. Reserved commit credits are account-scoped and prorated during handovers; exceptions are documented for incompatible model-family switches. For details, see attached pricing sheet."
